critique:
field selected_target, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  The failures occurred when a goal requested an ordinal placement and, after the cube was returned to the central workspace, demonstration targets moved and exchanged positions. The policy correctly chose to pick up the goal-colored cube, but stored the execution target nearest the original placement location. The annotations instead identified the moved target: for example, the first green-cube placement was on the lower target, which subsequently moved to [101, 166]. This breaks PREDICTABILITY because the existing rule mentions only occlusion and small coordinate shifts, not genuine target motion. Retain one field containing the first execution scene's center of the physical target selected by the requested chronological placement. Identify that target at the completed release, then follow its identity through the remainder of the demonstration, including large movements and exchanges of positions. Count releases exactly as before; target movement does not change the placement ordinal. Write the final matched execution-scene point at the first decision and retain it unchanged thereafter. For example, write [101, 166] for a selected lower target whose demonstrated motion ends at the image-right target. Remove the episode-specific lookup values and replace the small-shift-only identity guidance with this full-motion tracking rule.

field selected_target, POLICY PROMPT
  When the demonstration showed targets exchanging positions after the cube's placements, the policy chose the correct pickup but mapped the requested release location directly to the nearest target in the initial execution scene. Consequently its stored point differed from the annotated destination of the moving physical target. This is a PREDICTABILITY failure, not evidence that placement counting should change. With empty incoming memory and the demonstration visible, count completed target releases of the goal-colored cube chronologically and select the requested one. Then continue scanning every remaining demonstration observation to track that target's motion until execution begins. Associate successive target observations using continuous trajectories, accounting jointly for the other targets rather than independently matching the original placement coordinate to the final layout. Targets can exchange locations even when the final layout resembles the original layout. For example, a selected target can move from approximately [137, 104] through [115, 110] and [98, 135] to the image-right target, whose execution center is [101, 166]. Likewise, an upper target can move to the lower position, and an image-right target can move to the image-left position. Store only the selected target's execution-scene center, not these intermediate trajectories; all tracking occurs within the demonstration available at the first decision. On later decisions copy selected_target unchanged. Preserve the existing release-count exclusions and unknown handling when identity genuinely cannot be established.
